Token Exfiltration and Session Fixation [Information Disclosure, Spoofing, CWE-384] on API Gateway, Lambda Authorizer, CloudFront, STS: Tokens could be exfiltrated through MITM attacks, XSS vulnerabilities, or client-side malware. Once obtained, these tokens could be used to impersonate legitimate users. An attacker performs a MITM attack to capture access tokens in transit, then uses these tokens to make authenticated API calls to the system.

Insufficient Monitoring and Detection [Repudiation, Information Disclosure, CWE-778] on CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Lambda Functions, API Gateway, DynamoDB: Without proper logging and monitoring, attackers could perform reconnaissance, gain unauthorized access, or abuse elevated privileges without detection. An attacker gains access to the system and performs multiple failed role assumption attempts before succeeding, but the activity goes unnoticed due to insufficient monitoring.

Lambda Authorizer Single Point of Compromise [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-285] on Lambda Authorizer, API Gateway: A vulnerability in the Lambda authorizer could be exploited to bypass authentication checks or generate valid tokens for unauthorized users. An attacker finds a bug in the token validation logic of the Lambda authorizer that allows them to bypass signature verification.

DynamoDB Race Conditions and Data Integrity [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-362] on DynamoDB, Lambda Functions: Concurrent operations on the same DynamoDB items could lead to race conditions where access requests are processed incorrectly or access is not properly revoked. An attacker exploits a race condition to maintain access after revocation by quickly creating a new request while the revocation is being processed.
